arxiv-2111-08291.title: Switching Recurrent Kalman Networks
arxiv-2111-08291.creator: Giao Nguyen-Quynh, Philipp Becker, Chen Qiu, Maja Rudolph, Gerhard Neumann
arxiv-2111-08291.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Giao Nguyen-Quynh, Philipp Becker, Chen Qiu, Maja Rudolph, Gerhard Neumann. Forecasting driving behavior or other sensor measurements is an essential component of autonomous driving systems. Often real-world multivariate time series data is hard to model because the underlying dynamics are nonlinear and the observations are noisy. In addition, driving data can often be multimodal in distribution, meaning that there are distinct predictions that are likely, but averaging can hurt model performance.

arxiv-2209-06099.title: A solution to the degree- d d Twisted Rabbit Problem
arxiv-2209-06099.creator: Malavika Mukundan, Rebecca R. Winarski
arxiv-2209-06099.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Malavika Mukundan, Rebecca R. Winarski. We solve generalizations of Hubbard’s twisted rabbit problem for analogues of the rabbit polynomial of degree d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . The twisted rabbit problem asks: when a certain quadratic polynomial, called the Douady Rabbit polynomial, is twisted by a cyclic subgroup of a mapping class group, to which polynomial is the resulting map equivalent (as a function of the power of the generator)?

arxiv-2212-09450.title: Accelerating Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery with Latent Structure Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’23),
arxiv-2212-09450.creator: Danqing Wang, Zeyu Wen, Fei Ye, Lei Li, Hao Zhou
arxiv-2212-09450.description: Abstract . Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising therapeutic approaches against drug-resistant pathogens. Recently, deep generative models are used to discover new AMPs. However, previous studies mainly focus on peptide sequence attributes and do not consider crucial structure information. In this paper, we propose a latent sequence-structure model for designing AMPs ( LSSAMP ).

arxiv-2302-13073.title: Feedback Capacity of the Continuous-Time ARMA(1,1) Gaussian Channel
arxiv-2302-13073.creator: Jun Su Guangyue Han Shlomo Shamai (Shitz) The University of Hong Kong The University of Hong Kong Technion-Israel Institute of Technology email: junsu1995@connect.hku.hk email: ghan@hku.hk email: sshlomo@ee.technion.ac.il
arxiv-2302-13073.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jun Su Guangyue Han Shlomo Shamai (Shitz) The University of Hong Kong The University of Hong Kong Technion-Israel Institute of Technology email: junsu1995@connect.hku.hk email: ghan@hku.hk email: sshlomo@ee.technion.ac.il. We consider the continuous-time ARMA(1,1) Gaussian channel and derive its feedback capacity in closed form.

arxiv-2405-14649.title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Advanced Nanoscale X-ray Analysis: Unmixing Multicomponent Signals and Enhancing Chemical Quantification
arxiv-2405-14649.creator: Hui Chen, Duncan T.L. Alexander, Cécile Hébert
arxiv-2405-14649.description: Abstract Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy in the transmission electron microscope is a key tool for nanomaterials analysis, providing a direct link between spatial and chemical information. However, using it for precisely determining chemical compositions presents challenges of noisy data from low X-ray yields and mixed signals from phases that overlap along the electron beam trajectory.

arxiv-2408-01754.title: Impact of polarization mode dispersion on entangled photon distribution
arxiv-2408-01754.creator: Vadim Rodimin 1, *, Konstantin Kravtsov 1, Rui Ming Chua 1,2, Gianluca De Santis 1, Aleksei Ponasenko 1, Yury Kurochkin 1, Alexander Ling 2,3 and James A. Grieve 1
arxiv-2408-01754.description: Abstract The polarization mode dispersion (PMD) in optical fibers poses a major challenge for maintaining the fidelity of quantum states for quantum communications. In this work, a comprehensive model linking the probability of quantum measurement errors (infidelity) to PMD is developed and validated by experimental measurements of differential group delay and quantum bit error rate (QBER).

arxiv-2408-15229.title: Why are optical coronal lines faint in active galactic nuclei?
arxiv-2408-15229.creator: Jeffrey D. McKaig, Shobita Satyapal, Ari Laor, Nicholas P. Abel, Sara M. Doan, Claudio Ricci, Jenna M. Cann
arxiv-2408-15229.description: Abstract Forbidden collisionally excited optical atomic transitions from high ionization potential (IP ≥ \geq 54.8 eV) ions, such as Ca 4+ , Ne 4+ , Fe 6+ , Fe 10+ , Fe 13+ , Ar 9+ , and S 11+ , are known as optical coronal lines (CLs).

barruel-memoires-jacobinisme-t2-1798.title: Mémoires pour servir à l'histoire du Jacobinisme, Tome 2 (Hambourg, 1798)
barruel-memoires-jacobinisme-t2-1798.creator: Augustin Barruel
barruel-memoires-jacobinisme-t2-1798.description: Tome 2 of Barruel's Memoirs — the conspiracy against sovereigns and the Sophists of rebellion; completes the anti-philosophe half of the great conspiracy narrative.

plos-pone-0006409.description: PLOS ONE research article. Sepsis is a major healthcare problem and current estimates suggest that the incidence of sepsis is approximately 750,000 annually. Sepsis is caused by an inability of the immune system to eliminate invading pathogens. It was recently proposed that endogenous mediators produced du

pmc-10634015.title: Service delivery interventions to improve maternal and newborn health in low- and middle-income countries: scoping review of quality improvement, implementation research and health system strengthening approaches
pmc-10634015.creator: Solange Mianda, Olamide Todowede, Helen Schneider
pmc-10634015.description: IntroductionThis review explores the characteristics of service delivery-related interventions to improve maternal and newborn health (MNH) in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs) over the last two decades, comparing three common framings of these interventions, namely, quality improvement (QI), implementation science/research (IS/IR), and health system strengthening (HSS).MethodsThe review followed the staged scoping review methodology proposed by Levac et al. (2010).

pmc-11436036.title: Innovative Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rope-Based Closed-Form Retrofitting Methods Applied in Reinforced Concrete T-Shaped Beams under Torsion
pmc-11436036.creator: Adamantis G. Zapris, Violetta K. Kytinou, Constantin E. Chalioris
pmc-11436036.description: The fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) strengthening of reinforced concrete (RC) elements with torsional deficiencies has not yet been extensively studied. Existing studies have primarily focused on rectangular RC beams. The few studies on L or T-shaped beams have used open-form retrofitting methods. However, premature debonding of the retrofitting from concrete surfaces often leads to detachment before achieving enhanced torsional capacity.

pmc-11454784.title: 6866 Real-world implications and limitations of GLP-1 prescriptions in adolescents
pmc-11454784.creator: Gabriel Castano, Stephanie Sisley
pmc-11454784.description: Disclosure: G. Castano: None. S. Sisley: None. Background: Glucagon-like-peptide-1 agonists (GLP1), approved for adolescents ≥ 10 years in 2019 for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and ≥ 12 years in 2020 for obesity, require adequate dose titration and have known side effects.

pmc-11480150.title: Progression from Non-alcoholic Steatohepatitis to Advanced Liver Diseases and Mortality Among Medicare Patients
pmc-11480150.creator: Yestle Kim, Joe Medicis, Matthew Davis, Dominic Nunag, Robert Gish
pmc-11480150.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionNon-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) may progress to more advanced liver disease. This study aimed to characterize NASH progression and mortality in the Medicare population.MethodsPatients with NASH in 100% Medicare fee-for-service claims accrued from 2015–2021 who were ≥ 66 years old at index diagnosis, continuously enrolled for ≥ 12 months prior to and ≥ 6 months following index (unless death), and had no evidence of other causes of liver disease were included.

pmc-11522108.title: Performance on curriculum-based mathematics assessments in developmental dyscalculia: the effect of content domain and question format
pmc-11522108.creator: Alison Roulstone, Kinga Morsanyi, Julia Bahnmueller
pmc-11522108.description: Developmental Dyscalculia (DD) is characterised by persistent difficulties in learning mathematical skills, which usually becomes apparent in the early years of schooling. Traditionally, DD is known to affect children’s arithmetic processing, whilst other domains of mathematics receive much less research attention.

pmc-11678638.title: Size Effect on Shear Behaviors of 3D-Printed Soft Rock-like Materials Under Different Shear Velocities
pmc-11678638.creator: Chaolei Wu, Lishuai Jiang, Yang Zhao, Qi Wu, Yiming Yang, Xiaohan Peng, Pimao Li
pmc-11678638.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The shear failure of rock masses is one of the primary causes of underground engineering instability. The shear mechanical behavior of rocks at different sizes is of great significance for studying the shear failure pattern of engineering rock masses. However, due to the presence of various joints and defects in natural rocks, the obtained rock specimens exhibit significant discreteness, making it difficult to customize specimen sizes for size effect studies.

pmc-11689506.title: LIFE SATISFACTION MODERATES LIFESPAN DECLINES IN STRESS REACTIVITY
pmc-11689506.creator: William Chopik
pmc-11689506.description: Positive psychological well-being is often conceptualized as a protective factor for maintaining health across the lifespan. But why does psychological well-being confer such benefits? One potential possibility is that it shapes how we respond to stressors on a daily basis. However, much of existing research on this topic will examine these associations in the context of short-term experience sampling studies.

pmc-12452473.title: Bioinformation vortices and the emergence of plant life: A unified theory integrating prebiotic signal processing and evolutionary transitions
pmc-12452473.creator: Arunvel Thangamani, Deepavalli Arumuganainar
pmc-12452473.description: According to Information Vortex Theory, the spatially distributed wave energy associated with the constituent molecules of an incepting cell interacts with the surrounding space to generate a rotating bioinformation field, forming a vortex. This vortex, characterized as a local maximum of energy density, constitutes both inbound and outbound energy fluxes, corresponding to signal reception and dispersal, respectively.

pmc-12455087.title: A magnetotactic bacterium capable of magnetic sensing
pmc-12455087.creator: Emilie Gachon, Sascha Lambert, Sandrine Grosse, Elsa Turrini, Emma Ropion, Stefan Klumpp, Christopher T Lefèvre, Mila Sirinelli, Damien Faivre
pmc-12455087.description: SummaryMagnetosensitive organisms have the ability to sense and respond actively to features of magnetic fields such as the direction or magnitude. Until now, magnetosensing has been characterized primarily in higher organisms, involving either a cryptochrome-based mechanism or direct magnetic interactions with magnetic particles.

pmc-12569032.title: The predictive value of the vasoactive inotropic score in the postoperative treatment of patients suffering from infective endocarditis
pmc-12569032.creator: Philipp Schnackenburg, Christopher Ternka, Shekhar Saha, Dietmar Wassilowsky, Christine Kamla, Christoph Mueller, Konstanze Horke, Sven Peterss, Christian Hagl, Dominik Joskowiak
pmc-12569032.description: The study aimed to analyze the predictive value of the vasoactive inotropic score (VIS) in the postoperative treatment of patients undergoing valve surgery for infective endocarditis (IE). At our institution, 334 patients underwent valve surgery for IE from 01/2016 to 12/2022. Patients with postoperative MCS device were excluded from this study.

pmc-12591729.title: The potential use of hydroxyapatite from sea coral as a bone substitute: a systematic review
pmc-12591729.creator: Indra Wahyudi, Andi Tajrin, Husni Mubarak
pmc-12591729.description: Background Bone defects can result from trauma, neoplasms, infections, or congenital anomalies. A common strategy for managing these defects is bone grafting, which must meet three essential biological requirements: osteoconductivity, osteogenicity, and osteoinductivity. Bone graft materials may be sourced from either natural or synthetic origins.

pmc-12608847.title: RSV Monitoring in Germany: A Critical Overview of Available Surveillance Systems
pmc-12608847.creator: Lea J. Bayer, Christian Brösamle, Gordon Brestrich, Bahar Najafi, Christof von Eiff, Cornelia Hösemann, Holger Stepan, Gunther Gosch, Michael Wojcinski, Michael Abou-Dakn, Egbert Herting, Markus A. Rose, Martina Prelog, Rolf Kaiser
pmc-12608847.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory infections in young children, elderly people, and patients with underlying diseases. Solid data on its epidemiology and burden of disease are essential for the implementation of preventive strategies. This review provides for the first time a comprehensive overview on publicly available RSV surveillance resources in Germany.

pmc-12722219.title: Complex soliton wave patterns of Gross–Pitaevskii systems: application in quantum and optical engineering
pmc-12722219.creator: Muhammad Bilal, Yazen M Alawaideh, Shafqat Ur Rehman, Ioan-Lucian Popa, Bashar M Al-khamiseh, Hala Ghannam
pmc-12722219.description: The purpose of this work is to explore precise solutions, particularly soliton solutions, by fractionally analyzing the multicomponent Gross–Pitaevskii problem, a basic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Soliton solutions are essential for comprehending the complex system dynamics, providing insight into superfluidity, superconductivity, and related nonlinear effects. The complex fractional Gross–Pitaevskii equation is solved by considering the -derivative.

pmc-13232696.title: Impaired Treg Response and Subclinical Cardiac Dysfunction in Children Following SARS-CoV-2 Infection
pmc-13232696.creator: Costanza Di Chiara, Anna Cantarutti, Jolanda Sabatino, Domenico Sirico, Francesco Bonfante, Marthe Le Prevost, Danilo Buonsenso, Emma Concetta Manno, Francesco Carmona, Daniele Donà, Anita De Rossi, Giovanni Di Salvo, Maria Raffaella Petrara, Carlo Giaquinto
pmc-13232696.description: In a preliminary cohort of children recovering from asymptomatic or mild coronavirus disease 2019, subclinical cardiac contractility alterations were associated with reduced regulatory T cells, shorter telomeres and elevated inflammatory markers 3 months post-infection. These findings suggest that immune dysregulation may contribute to silent post-coronavirus disease 2019 cardiac dysfunction and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts with long-term follow-up.
